column1: # patch-markers.tsv -- the machine-checked form of docs/framework-patches.md's Verify column (NWP-20261020-04).
# build-device.sh runs check-patch-markers.py against this table AFTER `m` and the build-number assert, BEFORE
# signing, on the artifact that assert read (the target-files zip, or the product tree of a dev image build). A row
# whose literal is missing from the built artifact fails the build: an upstream sync can leave an anchor that still
# matches while the patch's own edit lands nowhere, the script exits 0, and nothing else notices.
# CI runs `check-patch-markers.py --self-check .`, which holds this table to the patch scripts (below).
# FORMAT. Tab-separated, four columns, '#' starts a comment line. NO leading or trailing space in any text: a
# column ends at the next tab.
# <patch basename> resolves to the script build-device.sh APPLIES, never to a same-named script elsewhere: a name in
#   its GOS_MANDATED_PATCHES list -> editions/diaspore/build/patches/<n>; otherwise editions/endospore/build/patches/<n>
#   (so telephony-per-user.sh is the Endospore copy); otherwise editions/endospore/devices/*/patches/<n>, where a
#   need/absent text must appear in EVERY device's copy.
# <artifact basename> is found by basename in the target-files zip, or under system/ system_ext/ product/ vendor/ of
#   a product tree; exactly one match is required. An .apk/.jar is read as a zip and every classes*.dex in it is
#   searched; any other artifact is searched as raw bytes. `-` for exempt.
#   need     the text MUST be present: a literal the patch writes into the source.
#   control  a STOCK literal that must be present: it proves the right bytes were read, so a missing `need` means
#            the patch is absent and not that the wrong file was opened.
#   absent   the text must NOT be present: the original text the patch replaces.
#   exempt   the patch has no artifact literal that meets the two rules below; <text> is the reason.
# MARKER RULES. (a) A `need` text is a literal the patch writes as ONE contiguous string constant (a Java string
# literal, one piece of a Rust format string between placeholders, a sepolicy token), copied from the SCRIPT, not
# from the register; where they disagree the script wins. (b) It is SPECIFIC to ONE patch: it contains a
# Nowhere-only token (nowhere, Nowhere, a NWP-/DIA- work id) and appears in no other applied script. services.jar
# carries the literals of about eight patches and `com.nowhere.chooser` is inserted by two of them, so a shared or
# generic text would let one patch's literal stand in for another's absence.
# A patch that inserts no such literal is exempt, with the reason. Every applied patch needs a row; a NEW patch is not
# done until it has one (docs/framework-patches.md, THE ONE RULE).
